title: Running Your First Program

content.title: The Code Editor
content.summary: The editor is where you type Python code.
content.body:
The editor is where you write Python programs. Click inside it and start typing.

It works a lot like a normal text editor, except instead of writing sentences or notes, you're writing instructions for Python to run.

content.title: The Run Button
content.summary: Press Run to make Python run your code from top to bottom.
content.body:
When you press Run, Python goes through your code one line at a time, from top to bottom, and follows each instruction.

Writing code by itself does nothing yet — your program only runs after you press Run.

content.title: The Output Panel
content.summary: Results and error messages appear in the Output panel.
content.body:
After your program runs, the results appear in the Output panel.

If something goes wrong, Python shows an error message to help you figure out what happened.

content.title: print() — Your First Command
content.summary: print("Hello!") displays text on the screen.
content.body:
print() tells Python to display a message on the screen.

print("Hello!")

The quotation marks are important — they tell Python where the message starts and ends.

Try changing "Hello!" to your own message, then press Run.

You can change the message and run the program as many times as you want.

steps.instruction: Step 1: Change the message inside the quotation marks. Before you press Run, try to predict what will appear in the output.
Step 2: Add a second print() line below the first. Python will run both lines from top to bottom.

bonusSteps.instruction: Bonus: Write 3 print() lines — give the computer a name, a job, and one silly fact about it.

progressiveHints:
# Hint: Use print() with a message inside quotation marks
print("I like pizza")

print("Hello, world!")
print("I made the computer say this!")
